Presentation Outline

WHAT WE ARE BUILDING, AND WHY

Project Objective and Research Question

Can morphological changes in PC12 cells following NGF treatment be quantified automatically and reproducibly from brightfield or phase-contrast images?

THE PROBLEM

Morphology is scored by eye — slow, subjective, not reproducible.

THE APPROACH

Standardise culture and imaging, then quantify with a repeatable pipeline.

THE OUTCOME

A traceable dataset and a method that compares before and after NGF.

Soma

Count · area · shape · confluence

Neurites

Count · length · orientation

Branching

Differentiation

Comparison across NGF conditions — control vs NGF days

Quality metadata

Well · position · replicate · acquisition settings

WHY PC12, AND WHY THIS MATTERS

The PC12 Model

PC12 is a rat adrenal pheochromocytoma cell line. Given NGF, it stops dividing and extends neurites, adopting a sympathetic neuron-like phenotype.

1

The Model

Inexpensive, fast-growing and reproducible. It gives a neuronal readout without primary neuron culture.

2

The Signal

NGF drives neurite outgrowth. Length, count and branching change measurably — that change is the data.

3

Why It Matters

Neurite outgrowth is a standard readout in neurotoxicity and drug screening. Scoring it by hand is the bottleneck.

Pre-warm the medium

WHAT
Growth medium prepared and warmed to 37 °C before the vial leaves the freezer.
WHY
Otherwise the thawed cells sit waiting in DMSO.
MEDIUM37 °CReady before thawing starts

02/ 10

Vial out of the freezer

WHAT
1 mL cryovial. Cells frozen in 90% FBS + 10% DMSO: 900 µL + 100 µL per mL.
WHY
DMSO prevents ice-crystal damage, but it is toxic once warm.
STORED AT−80 °C90% FBS + 10% DMSO

03/ 10

Thaw in the hand

WHAT
Held in the hand until the ice melted.
NOTE
A 37 °C water bath is the faster standard. Slower thawing means longer DMSO contact.
THAWING
OURS · SLOWER
In the hand
STANDARD · FASTER
37 °C water bath

04/ 10

Dilute in the vial

WHAT
Medium pipetted into the vial and mixed up and down.
WHY
The DMSO starts diluting right where the cells are.
DMSODilutingStarts inside the 1 mL vial

05/ 10

Transfer to a Falcon tube

WHAT
Suspension moved into a Falcon tube that already held medium.
WHY
So the dilution continues instead of reversing.
DMSOStill dilutingMedium already in the tube

06/ 10

Centrifuge

WHAT
Spun at 1,250 rpm for 7 min. The cells collect as a pellet.
WHY
It separates the cells from the liquid that holds the DMSO.
SPIN1,250 rpm7 min

07/ 10

Pour off the supernatant

WHAT
The supernatant is poured off; the pellet stays in the tube.
WHY
It carries the remaining DMSO away. This is what the spin was for.
DMSORemovedWith the supernatant

08/ 10

Rinse the flask

WHAT
PBS added to the culture flask, cap closed, swirled across the base, then emptied.
RINSE WITHPBSBefore the cells go in

09/ 10

Resuspend the pellet

WHAT
Pellet resuspended in fresh medium by slow pipetting.
WHY
It gives a single-cell suspension, not clumps.
GOAL

10/ 10

Seed and incubate

WHAT
Flask labelled and seeded, then incubated at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
THEN
Medium renewed every 3 days from here.
INCUBATOR37 °C5% CO2

Sterile Technique

  1. Cabinet

    • UV cycle before the session
    • HEPA laminar flow running throughout
    • 70% ethanol wipe, before and after

  2. Entry

    • Every bottle, pipette, tube and rack: 70% ethanol on the way in

  3. Handling

    • Sterile single-use consumables
    • Never over an open vessel; close it after each transfer
    • Gloves re-sterilised between steps
